title: 光敏电阻测光：固定电阻该选多大
summary: 光敏电阻 + 固定电阻分压接到 Blue Pill 的 PA0（ADC）。先用一个太大的电阻，看亮处的读数挤成一团；再算出该用多大的。
concepts: 灵敏度与几何平均 sensitivity & geometric mean
ADC 模拟输入 analog input
description: Blue Pill 用 USB 供电。3V3 → 光敏电阻 LDR1 → 结点 VLIGHT → R1（6.8 kΩ）→ GND；VLIGHT 接一个 ADC 引脚（PA0–PA7、PB0、PB1），引脚设成模拟输入。光照在 1、10、100、1000 lux 之间变化。

cards.title: 先用一个太大的电阻
text: **Blue Pill** 的 **3V3** 接上方 + 轨，**GND** 接 − 轨。
搭一个分压器：+ 轨 → **光敏电阻** → 中点 → **`100 kΩ`** → GND。中点接 **PA0**，把 PA0 设成 **ADC**。
单击光敏电阻，在「属性」里把光照从 **`100 lux`** 拖到 **`1000 lux`**，看引脚列表里的 ADC 读数。
亮度变了 10 倍，读数为什么几乎不动？

cards.title: 两个电阻差不多大时最灵敏
text: - 光敏电阻**越亮，电阻越小**：亮度每变 10 倍，电阻大约变 5 倍。
![](fig:ldr)
- 分压器的输出在 **$R_1 = R_{LDR}$** 时变化最快，那一点正好是电源的一半。R1 太大，亮处的读数就全挤在 3.3 V 附近。
![](fig:div)
- 要照顾 1–1000 lux 整段，就取两端阻值的**几何平均**：
$$R_1 = \sqrt{R_{dark} × R_{bright}}$$
- 代入数字：1 lux 时约 75 kΩ，1000 lux 时约 0.6 kΩ，$R_1 = \sqrt{75 × 0.6} ≈ 6.7$ kΩ，取标准值 **6.8 kΩ**。

cards.title: 换成 6.8 kΩ
text: - 点**「检查我的电路」**。通过后，按题目把光照设成不同的值，用万用表测中点对 GND。
- 先预测：用 $R_{LDR} = 15 kΩ × (lux / 10)^{-0.7}$ 算出光敏电阻，再用分压公式。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **固定电阻 ≈ 你关心的亮度下的 $R_{LDR}$ 时最灵敏**；要覆盖一大段亮度，就取两端阻值的几何平均。
- 光敏电阻在上：越亮电压越高。换到下面就反过来，固件的判断也要跟着反过来。
- 坑：光敏电阻慢、个体差异大（±50 % 很常见），还随温度漂移，只适合分“亮 / 暗”。做“天黑开灯”要用两个阈值，否则灯在阈值附近会闪。
- STM32 的模拟引脚不耐 5 V：分压器接 3V3，不要接 5V。

caption.text: 每往右一格，光照变 10 倍，光敏电阻大约只剩 1/5。暗处是几十千欧，亮处不到 1 千欧。

i18n.en: Each step to the right is ten times the light, and the LDR drops to about a fifth. Tens of kilohms in the dark, under one kilohm in bright light.

caption.text: 光敏电阻在上、R1 在下，中点 VLIGHT 接 PA0：越亮 R_LDR 越小，V_PA0 越高。

i18n.en: LDR on top, R1 below, the middle node VLIGHT to PA0: the brighter it is, the smaller R_LDR and the higher V_PA0.

en.startNote: **Half-built**: the Blue Pill (PA0 already set to ADC) and the GND and 3V3 rails are wired. **Why**: powering the board is a repeated skill; the sensor divider is the lesson. **Your job**: the LDR from the 3V3 rail to column 22, R1 (6.8kΩ) from column 22 to GND, then column 22 to PA0 (a16).
en.title: An LDR light sensor: how big should the fixed resistor be?
en.summary: An LDR and a fixed resistor form a divider into the Blue Pill's PA0 (ADC). First use a resistor that is too big and watch the bright readings bunch up; then work out the right one.
en.description: The Blue Pill runs from USB. 3V3 → LDR1 → node VLIGHT → R1 (6.8 kΩ) → GND; VLIGHT goes to an ADC pin (PA0–PA7, PB0, PB1) set to analog input. The light changes between 1, 10, 100 and 1000 lux.
compare: **Compare**: If the reading moves the wrong way with light, check which of the LDR and R1 is on top. The working:
**LDR model** (GL5528-like): R_LDR = 15 kΩ × (lux / 10)^−0.7. Every 10× in light changes the resistance by 10^0.7 ≈ 5×:
- 1 lux (very dark) ≈ 75 kΩ; 10 lux ≈ 15 kΩ; 100 lux (indoors) ≈ 3.0 kΩ; 1000 lux (by a window / overcast outdoors) ≈ 600 Ω.
**Divider output**: V = 3.3 × R1 / (R1 + R_LDR). With the LDR on top, **brighter means higher voltage**:
Each 10× step in light moves the reading by about 940, 1570 and 920 counts — all three decades are clearly resolved.

**Why 6.8 kΩ**: the divider's sensitivity to ln(R_LDR) is greatest when **R1 = R_LDR** (V = Vcc/2 there, the steepest part of the curve). To cover 1–1000 lux, take the **geometric mean** of the two end resistances: √(75 kΩ × 0.6 kΩ) ≈ 6.7 kΩ → standard **6.8 kΩ**. If you only care about one light level (say 10 lux for "turn the lights on at dusk"), use the LDR's resistance there (≈ 15 kΩ). Compare:
- R1 = **100 kΩ**: 1.88 V / 2.87 V / 3.20 V / 3.28 V — the bright end is crammed at the top; 100 lux and 1000 lux differ by only 0.08 V.
- R1 = **1 kΩ**: 0.04 V / 0.21 V / 0.83 V / 2.07 V — the dark end is crammed near 0 V.

**Swap the positions**: put the LDR at the bottom (3V3 → R1 → VLIGHT → LDR → GND) and **brighter means lower voltage**; same sensitivity rule, opposite direction. Your firmware's bright/dark test must match the wiring.
**Current**: brightest 3.3 V / (6.8 k + 0.6 k) ≈ **0.45 mA**, darkest about 40 µA.

measurements.ask: 1 lux (very dark): multimeter on the ADC pin (VLIGHT) to GND
100 lux (indoors): the ADC pin to GND
measurements.explain: R_LDR ≈ 3.0 kΩ: 3.3 × 6.8 / 9.8 ≈ 2.29 V. With the LDR on top, brighter means higher.

measurements.ask: From your 100 lux reading, work back to the LDR's resistance R_LDR = R1 × (3.3 − V) / V
measurements.explain: ≈ 3.0 kΩ = 15 kΩ × 10^−0.7. Firmware does exactly this to get the resistance, then converts it to lux.

measurements.ask: 1000 lux (by a window): the ADC pin to GND
measurements.explain: R_LDR ≈ 600 Ω: 3.3 × 6.8 / 7.4 ≈ 3.03 V. 1, 10, 100 and 1000 lux are hundreds to over a thousand counts apart: all three decades are resolved.

measurements.ask: What happens if R1 is changed to 1 kΩ? (Try swapping it on the board.)
choices: the dark readings all crowd near 0 V, and 1 lux and 10 lux become almost indistinguishable
the bright readings all crowd near 3.3 V
all readings scale down and resolve just as well
measurements.explain: With 1 kΩ the four light levels give about 0.04 / 0.21 / 0.83 / 2.07 V: the dark end crowds near 0 V. The opposite of 100 kΩ — too big crowds the top, too small the bottom; the geometric mean, 6.8 kΩ, serves both ends.

hints: Wire a board 3V3 pin to the top + rail and a GND pin to the − rail first.
LDR from 3V3 to the middle node, 6.8 kΩ from the middle node to GND; the middle node goes to PA0 (or another ADC pin).
Set that pin to analog input (ADC) in the pin table.
tests: 1 lux: sensible ADC reading and LDR current
1000 lux: sensible ADC reading and LDR current

cards.title: Start with a resistor that is too big
text: Connect the **Blue Pill**'s **3V3** to the top + rail and **GND** to the − rail.
Build a divider: + rail → **LDR** → middle node → **`100 kΩ`** → GND. Wire the middle node to **PA0** and set PA0 to **ADC**.
Click the LDR and, under Properties, drag the light from **`100 lux`** to **`1000 lux`** while you watch the ADC reading in the pin list.
Ten times the light — why does the reading hardly move?

cards.title: Most sensitive when the two are about equal
text: - An LDR's resistance **falls as the light rises**: ten times the light, about a fifth of the resistance.
![](fig:ldr)
- A divider's output changes fastest when **$R_1 = R_{LDR}$**; at that point it sits at half the supply. With R1 too big, all the bright readings bunch up near 3.3 V.
![](fig:div)
- To cover the whole 1–1000 lux, take the **geometric mean** of the resistances at the two ends:
$$R_1 = \sqrt{R_{dark} × R_{bright}}$$
- With numbers: about 75 kΩ at 1 lux and about 0.6 kΩ at 1000 lux, $R_1 = \sqrt{75 × 0.6} ≈ 6.7$ kΩ; take the standard value **6.8 kΩ**.

cards.title: Swap in 6.8 kΩ
text: - **Replace** the `100 kΩ` with **`6.8 kΩ`** and leave the rest.
- Press **Check my circuit**. Once it passes, set the light to the values the questions ask for and measure the middle node to GND.
- Predict first: get the LDR's resistance from $R_{LDR} = 15 kΩ × (lux / 10)^{-0.7}$, then use the divider formula.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **The divider is most sensitive when the fixed resistor ≈ $R_{LDR}$ at the light level you care about**; to cover a wide range, take the geometric mean of the two ends.
- LDR on top: brighter means a higher voltage. Put it at the bottom and it reverses — and the firmware's test must reverse with it.

- The catch: LDRs are slow, vary a lot from part to part (±50 % is common) and drift with temperature; they are good for "light / dark" only. A "lights on at dusk" circuit needs two thresholds, or the lamp flickers around the switching point.
- The STM32's analog pins are not 5 V tolerant: feed the divider from 3V3, never from 5V.

tests.name: 1 lux：ADC 读数和光敏电阻电流合理
1000 lux：ADC 读数和光敏电阻电流合理

compare: **对比**：读数随光照变化的方向和预期相反时，检查光敏电阻和 R1 的位置。计算过程：
**光敏电阻模型**（GL5528 类）：R_LDR = 15 kΩ × (lux / 10)^−0.7。亮度每变 10 倍，电阻变 10^0.7 ≈ 5 倍：
- 1 lux（很暗）≈ 75 kΩ；10 lux ≈ 15 kΩ；100 lux（室内）≈ 3.0 kΩ；1000 lux（窗边 / 阴天户外）≈ 600 Ω。
**分压结果**：V = 3.3 × R1 / (R1 + R_LDR)。光敏电阻在上，**越亮电压越高**：
每 10 倍亮度读数差约 940、1570、920 个计数——整个 3 个数量级都分得很清楚。

**为什么选 6.8 kΩ**：分压器输出对 ln(R_LDR) 的灵敏度在 **R1 = R_LDR** 时最大（那一点 V = Vcc/2，曲线最陡）。要覆盖 1–1000 lux，就取两端阻值的**几何平均**：√(75 kΩ × 0.6 kΩ) ≈ 6.7 kΩ → 标准值 **6.8 kΩ**。如果只关心某一个亮度附近（比如“天黑开灯”的 10 lux），就选那个亮度下的 R_LDR（≈ 15 kΩ）。对比：
**换个位置**：把光敏电阻放到下面（3V3 → R1 → VLIGHT → LDR → GND），就变成**越亮电压越低**；灵敏度规律一样，只是方向反过来。固件里怎么判断“亮 / 暗”要和接法对应。

measurements.ask: 1 lux（很暗）：万用表测 ADC 引脚（VLIGHT）对 GND

measurements.explain: R_LDR ≈ 3.0 kΩ：3.3 × 6.8 / 9.8 ≈ 2.29 V。光敏电阻在上，越亮电压越高。

measurements.ask: 用你的 100 lux 读数反算光敏电阻的阻值 R_LDR = R1 × (3.3 − V) / V
measurements.explain: ≈ 3.0 kΩ = 15 kΩ × 10^−0.7。固件就是这样从读数算出电阻、再换成照度的。
R_LDR ≈ 600 Ω：3.3 × 6.8 / 7.4 ≈ 3.03 V。1、10、100、1000 lux 之间读数都差几百上千个计数，3 个数量级都分得开。

choices: 暗处的读数全挤在 0 V 附近，1 lux 和 10 lux 几乎分不开
亮处的读数全挤在 3.3 V 附近
读数整体按比例变小，分辨能力一样
measurements.ask: 如果把 R1 换成 1 kΩ，会怎样？（可以在面包板上换一下试试）
measurements.explain: 1 kΩ 时四个亮度分别约 0.04 / 0.21 / 0.83 / 2.07 V：暗处挤在 0 V 附近。和 100 kΩ 正好相反——R1 太大挤在顶上，太小挤在底下，几何平均 6.8 kΩ 两头都照顾到。

hints: 先把开发板的 3V3 接到上方 + 轨、GND 接到 − 轨。
光敏电阻从 3V3 接到中点，6.8 kΩ 从中点接到 GND；中点接 PA0（或别的 ADC 引脚）。
在引脚表里把这个引脚设成“模拟输入 ADC”。
startNote: **半成品**：Blue Pill（PA0 已设成 ADC）、GND 和 3V3 电源轨已经接好。**为什么**：板子的供电是重复技能；这里要学的是传感器分压。**你要做**：光敏电阻从 3V3 轨接到第 22 列，R1（6.8kΩ）从第 22 列接到 GND，再把第 22 列接到 PA0（a16）。
